audit_findings.title: Tax Receivable Agreement liability is an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $683 million latest filed payable; $3.40 per share and 8.9% of base equity value on an undiscounted bridge screen
audit_findings.evidence: As of February 1, 2026, the Company had recorded a $720 million payable to related parties pursuant to the Tax Receivable Agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q demonstrates a $683 million TRA payable, comprising $41 million current and $642 million non-current, while the valuation bridge includes no TRA claim. The payments are financing outflows excluded from owner earnings, whereas the related cash-tax savings can increase operating cash flow. A mechanical $683 million deduction would reduce base value from $38.21 to $34.81 per share and bull value from $44.95 to $41.55, changing the bull comparison with the $44.32 market price. The precise economic deduction may differ because payment timing and retained tax benefits must be matched.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile forecast cash-tax savings and TRA payments year by year, discount the scheduled $683 million payments at the required return, and rerun the bridge without double-counting tax benefits; separately model the filed potential $75 million liability from a full remaining Partnership Interest exchange.

audit_findings.title: Combined claim denominator may omit NCI tax-distribution cash costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $7 million paid in fiscal 2025 and $2 million in first-quarter fiscal 2026; a conditional recurring $7 million deduction equals 1.3% of the $536 million anchor and approximately $0.49 per share of base value
audit_findings.evidence: In addition to making distributions to Core & Main, Inc. to fund tax obligations and payments under the Tax Receivable Agreements, in accordance with the Partnership Agreement, Holdings also makes distributions to Management Feeder representing the non-controlling interests of Core & Main, Inc. to fund their income tax obligations with various taxing authorities.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributions are demonstrated, but a valuation error is not. If consolidated owner earnings are divided by a denominator containing the corresponding Partnership Interests, cash distributed to those holders is a return to claims represented in the denominator rather than leakage. If the numerator or denominator excludes those holders inconsistently, value would be overstated. The supplied valuation has no owner-earnings build or defined perimeter, so the record cannot establish whether the claims are matched; the potential adjustment is also close to the narrow bull-case premium over market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct the 201.021848 million-share denominator and the $536 million owner-earnings numerator by ownership class. Confirm that consolidated OE is paired with all Class A-equivalent Partnership Interests, or rerun using Core & Main-attributable OE and a Class A-only fully diluted denominator, including any required distribution true-ups.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: forecast impact unquantified; filed net acquisition cash outflows were $231 million in fiscal 2023, $741 million in fiscal 2024 and $61 million in fiscal 2025
audit_findings.evidence: Net sales increased primarily due to a 4.8% increase in average daily net sales driven by higher volumes and acquisitions partially offset by one less selling week compared to prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: Acquisition spending is excluded from the owner-earnings anchor while acquired operations contribute to earnings. The filings identify acquisitions as a contributor to fiscal-2025 growth and as offsetting decreased volume in first-quarter fiscal 2026, so free acquisition-supported growth is a credible concern. However, the filings do not separate organic growth or quantify the acquisition spending required to sustain the 3% and 6% scenarios. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the supplied record, although historical spending shows it could be large relative to the $536 million anchor.
audit_findings.action: Obtain organic sales and earnings growth excluding acquisitions, estimate normalized recurring acquisition consideration needed for each scenario, and rerun the base and bull cases either with that spending deducted from OE or with growth limited to the rate supported by already-deducted reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration may be missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $14 million latest filed fair-value liability, equal to $0.07 per share and 0.18% of base equity value; contractual maximum $18 million, equal to $0.09 per share and 0.23% of base equity value
audit_findings.evidence: On the acquisition date and as of February 1, 2026, the fair value of the contingent consideration liability was estimated at $14 million by utilizing a weighted probability assessment of the potential outcomes (a level 3 fair value measurement based on unobservable inputs).
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q continues to report $14 million of deferred consideration, demonstrating that the claim remained outstanding. Its omission modestly overstates equity value, but even the $18 million contractual maximum is only about $0.09 per share and does not change the base valuation, market-price conclusion or buy-below decision.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the $14 million liability is not already captured in another bridge or owner-earnings item, then deduct the surviving fair-value amount from the equity bridge and monitor subsequent remeasurement or payment.
